name: AzureBlobList
caption: Azure Blob: List files

configuration.description: Code of an AutoFlow Credential (max 20 chars; longer values are cut, matching is not case-sensitive). Its authentication type must be 'OAuth 2.0 client credentials' (Entra app, scope https://storage.azure.com/.default) or 'Azure Storage SAS token'. Credentials are company data and are NOT part of the flow definition – the code must exist in the target company.

Storage account name (3-24 lowercase letters/digits), e.g. contosodocs for https://contosodocs.blob.core.windows.net. Trimmed. May contain SmartFields; the resolved value is checked when the step runs.
Blob container name (3-63 chars, lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens, starting/ending with letter or digit; $root and $web also accepted). Trimmed. SmartFields allowed.
Path prefix; lists files whose path starts with this text (e.g. invoices/2026/). Empty = whole container. Trimmed, backslashes become slashes, a leading slash is dropped.
Only files directly inside the folder named by path (a trailing '/' is appended to a non-empty path), not files in sub-folders.

Index-tag conditions, AND-combined: array of {"tag": string, "op": "="|">"|">="|"<"|"<=", "value": string}. Rows with an empty tag are ignored; empty op means '='. value supports SmartText. When at least one filter is present the step uses Azure's find-by-tags query, which spans the whole storage account; hits are then narrowed to the configured container and to path (and directly inside it when folderLevelOnly).
Stop after this many files. <= 0 (or absent) means 500; values above 5000 are capped at 5000.
Also return each file's index tags (needs Storage Blob Data Owner, or a SAS with the Tags permission). Ignored for tag-filter queries.
Raise an error when no file is found.

outputs.name: results
outputs.when: only when at least one file is found

rules.check: configuration.credentialCode must be non-empty. The editor marks the field as required ("Please fill in the highlighted fields."); at run time an empty code fails the step with this message.
rules.message: Select a credential for the Azure Blob Storage connection.

rules.check: The credential must exist in the company. Also shown as an advisory on the editor's status line (prefixed with ⚠); it does not block saving.
The credential's authentication type must be 'OAuth 2.0 client credentials' or 'Azure Storage SAS token'. Also shown as an advisory on the editor's status line (prefixed with ⚠).
rules.message: Credential %1 uses the authentication type "%2". Azure Blob Storage steps accept "%3" (an Entra app) or "%4".

rules.check: Editor status line only (advisory, prefixed with ⚠, does not block saving): an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials credential's scope should contain 'storage.azure.com'. Not checked at run time; a wrong scope surfaces as an Azure authentication error.
rules.message: Credential %1 requests the scope "%2". Azure Blob Storage needs a token for the scope https://storage.azure.com/.default.

rules.check: The resolved storageAccount (trimmed) must be 3-24 chars of a-z and 0-9; an empty value also fails. Checked when the step runs, before any Azure call. The editor does not check the format. The machine check skips values containing '{{'.
rules.message: The storage account name "%1" is not valid. It must be 3 to 24 characters long and contain only lowercase letters and digits.

rules.check: The resolved container (trimmed) must be $root, $web, or 3-63 chars of a-z, 0-9 and single hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen; an empty value also fails. Checked when the step runs. The editor does not check the format. The machine check skips values containing '{{'.
rules.message: The container name "%1" is not valid. It must be 3 to 63 characters long and contain only lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

rules.check: Each tagFilters[].op should be one of =, >, >=, <, <= (the editor only offers these; no code check exists – any other text is passed to Azure verbatim and Azure rejects it).
rules.message: (no message – enforced by the editor's option column)

rules.check: A SAS-token credential must have a token stored.
rules.message: Credential %1 has no SAS token stored.

rules.check: If the credential has base URLs (an allow-list), https://<storageAccount>.blob.core.windows.net/<container> must start with one of them. Also shown as an advisory on the editor status line when account and container are literal.
rules.message: The URL "%1" is not allowed by credential "%2". Allowed prefixes: %3.

rules.check: errorOnEmpty = true and no file found.
rules.message: No files were found in container %1 under "%2".

notes: Each listed file is stored as an Azure Blob Entry row (table 5564412; fields include Name, Path, Parent Directory, Size, Content Type, Created At, Last Modified, ETag, Tags, Metadata, Storage Account, Container). results points at the first row; results[0], results[1], ... address each row individually; For Each over {{<slug>_results}} iterates them. When nothing is found, results is not written at all (count = 0).

The rows belong to the top-level execution (also when listed inside a SubFlow) and are deleted when that execution succeeds or is deleted. A failed execution keeps them so a restart can reuse them. Rows created outside an execution (editor test run) are never cleaned up automatically.

Azure error codes are translated: BlobNotFound, ContainerNotFound ('The container %1 was not found in storage account %2.'), Authorization* ('Azure denied access to container %1 (%2). ...'), AuthenticationFailed/InvalidAuthenticationInfo/NoAuthenticationInformation ('Azure could not authenticate the request (%1). ...'); anything else becomes 'Listing files failed: <Azure text>'.
Required Azure roles: Storage Blob Data Reader to list; Storage Blob Data Owner to read index tags.
Find-by-tags results carry only what Azure's find-by-tags response returns (name, matched tags); size, content type and dates may be empty for those rows.

There is no publish-time check for this step. In the editor only the required fields (credentialCode, storageAccount, container) and the advisory status line (credential exists, type, OAuth scope, URL allow-list) apply; every other check runs when the step runs.
